The @CIDH (IACHR)'s landmark decision recognizing the Cuban state’s responsibility for abuses against @CubalexDDHH is an important victory for accountability and human rights defenders across the region. The findings expose the costs of Cuban repression and reaffirm that those documenting human rights abuses deserve protection, not persecution. #Cuba #HumanRights Cubalex (@CubalexDDHH) ⚖️ La Comisión Interamericana responsabiliza al Estado cubano por violaciones de derechos humanos contra la organización Cubalex El Centro de Información Legal Cubalex y el Robert & Ethel Kennedy Human Rights Center celebran la histórica decisión publicada hoy por la Comisión Interamericana de Derechos Humanos (CIDH), mediante la cual se declara la responsabilidad del Estado cubano por la vigilancia ilegal, el hostigamiento, la represión y la detención arbitraria de los abogados y el personal de la organización. Este fallo es el resultado de más de ocho años de litigio estratégico. La CIDH emitió múltiples recomendaciones obligatorias al Estado de Cuba, exigiendo la reparación integral a las víctimas —incluyendo compensación económica, medidas de satisfacción y condiciones para el retorno seguro de quienes fueron forzados al exilio—, la investigación y sanción de los funcionarios responsables, y la adopción de medidas legislativas y administrativas para erradicar la violencia y la criminalización contra defensores de derechos humanos. Desde su fundación en La Habana en 2010, Cubalex ha brindado asistencia jurídica gratuita y documentado abusos estatales, enfrentando por ello una severa persecución. Entre 2012 y 2016, sus miembros sufrieron detenciones bajo cargos fabricados, intervención de comunicaciones y restricciones de viaje. La represión escaló en septiembre de 2016 con un violento allanamiento sin orden judicial a su sede, donde se incautaron equipos y archivos, forzando al exilio a la mayor parte del equipo. El abogado Julio Ferrer Tamayo permaneció detenido arbitrariamente hasta 2017 y logró exiliarse en 2024. La CIDH concluyó que el régimen cubano violó los derechos a la privacidad, debido proceso, libertad de expresión, reunión, asociación, tránsito y protección contra el arresto arbitrario. Asimismo, determinó que el Estado provocó daños físicos y psicológicos intencionales en represalia directa por la labor de Cubalex, con el fin de impedir la defensa de los derechos humanos dentro de un marco jurídico y político que sigue siendo abiertamente represivo. #Cubalex #DerechosHumanos #CIDH #Justicia #Cuba #SOSCuba #RendiciónDeCuentas — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/CubalexDDHH/status/2079598428217110685#m

Russian media reports that Putin has signed a decree to increase the Russian Armed Forces by 27,000 military personnel starting August 1. The stated reason was the "creation of military-construction units," and of course, everyone believed it.

For the past six months, the Ukrainian 🇺🇦 army has been on the offensive along a 50-kilometer-wide front, gradually retaking villages lost the previous year. With no official statements and very few videos available, little is known about this "offensive." I have therefore gathered as much information as possible to discuss it. In 2025, the Russian army doubled its rate of advance compared to 2024. Yet, it was not in the Donbas that they were advancing the most. Very early in the year, they seized Velyka Novosilka and pushed north toward Komar and west toward Huliaipole. By the year's end, the situation for Ukraine was critical: defensive lines facing south had been overrun from the east, and the Russian army was steadily closing in on Zaporizhzhia, a city of 800,000 inhabitants. After the capture of Huliaipole, everyone expected Pokrovsk'e, Ternuvate (already infiltrated at the time), and then Orikhiv to fall, placing the Russian army at the gates of Zaporizhzhia by the end of the year. Yet, seven months later, the situation remained unchanged; the Russians are still stalled west of Huliaipole. Worse, they have lost significant territory further north, bringing a halt to this offensive, which, while secondary to the main Donbas campaign, had nonetheless committed a massive force, including five armies and an army corps. 🔸So, what happened? It began in February, when several air-assault brigades repositioned to the region, launched an armored assault under cover of fog, deploying their infantry into contested villages, often behind the initial Russian infiltrators. The villages were methodically cleared, and Ukrainian soldiers began infiltrating southward themselves. In March, they were positioned east and west of Uspenivka, blocking Russian attempts to advance toward Pokrovske and Ternuvate. In response to this offensive, the Russian army sends several naval infantry brigades and divisions, as well as the 68th Army Corps, as reinforcements. Starting in April, air assault brigades repositioned further north with the mission of advancing on Komar. The goal of this redeployment was to prevent the 90th Tank Division from shifting its assets toward Dobropilla. There was no mechanized offensive this time, as the terrain, specifically the presence of several rivers, most notably the Vovtcha, precluded it. Instead, small Ukrainian infantry groups managed to gradually infiltrate as far as the next river, the Mokri Yali. It is important to understand that, despite having been in the area for at least eight months, Russian forces had been unable to consolidate their positions; a network of rivers complicated logistics, and the small size of the villages made it impossible to concentrate large numbers of troops. Consequently, the Ukrainians were able to advance relatively stealthily behind enemy lines, reaching the Mokri Yali River. A strict information blackout was imposed in the area. Apart from a single video (since deleted) showing Ukrainian troops raising a flag over a liberated village, the Ukrainians released nothing regarding an operation that had already been underway for three months. For their part, the Russians continued to obscure the situation: the Vostok Group released only videos that were difficult to geolocate and persisted in sending "suicide" flag-bearers troops, who would reach Iskra and raise the Russian flag, creating an illusion of control. On the map, I have roughly depicted the situation as it has stood over the last few weeks, relying primarily on a handful of geolocated videos, satellite imagery showing air and artillery strikes, and scattered social media statements. Simply put, little is known about the actual state of the front, other than the fact that Ukrainian forces are at the gates of Komar, a move that has forced the 90th Tank Division to keep half its strength committed to that sector. What I am certain of is that all Russian troops positioned north of the Vovcha River (in Ivanivka) or the Solena (in Novopavlivka) have either been killed or captured, judging by the number of Russian air strikes, at least a hundred, carried out in the area. Consequently, the section of the "New Donbass Line" in this sector has held for the tenth consecutive month. It is certain that the Ukrainians have retaken control of the few villages to the south, given the air strikes observed in the zone. For the time being, I will respect Ukrainian OPSEC protocols and refrain from providing further details regarding an ongoing operation, as long as more confirmation are not coming. 🔸You might be wondering how such an operation is structured. The Ukrainians are making extensive use of drones to establish a wide exclusion zone in the sector, extending particularly along the river as far as Velyka Novosilka. The operation is proceeding cautiously, with small infantry teams advancing gradually, supported by artillery positioned in the woods to the west and occasional Ukrainian air strikes on Russian drone operator positions in Komar. Overall, it is important to understand that this operation is taking place because the Russian army is unable to bring reinforcements to the front. Furthermore, anti-tank ditches prevent any Russian mechanized or motorized assault aimed at delivering reinforcements. To understand the disarray within the local command, one need only look at its use of air power. Air strikes are being carried out daily deep behind the lines, as far as Prossiana and Chaplyne, 35 to 40 km from the front. While the goal is to hinder the Ukrainian presence, these strikes primarily highlight the ineffectiveness of Russian drones in the sector, particularly the Molniya models. To conclude, this operation not only gained time for Ukraine to further fortify the Pavlohrad direction, it is a direct push in the foot of Russian forces, which can continue further this summer and later in the autumn. I'll continue to monitor this and wait for more official informations regarding the situation here. Thank you for reading !
